items.title: Inclusion is an invitation to someone else’s table
items.summary: You ask what these contradictions say about solidarity. I will make two points, and then I will say what I think it takes to move beyond visibility and inclusion. Every movement has a default First. Every movement has a default. One group is taken to speak for all. In the anti-racist movement, it was often Black men. In the women’s movement here, it was often dominant-caste Savarna women. In our movement, the anti-caste movement, it is often Dalit men who are cisgender and heterosexual. I say “our” because I am part of this movement. This is not an attack. It is a question we must ask ourselves. At the walk, I took a small pride flag and held it in front of my face. The flag was the size of a handkerchief. It did not really cover me. My anxiety was bigger than the flag. items.title: Supreme Court orders ₹30 lakh compensation to man kept in jail for over 7 years despite acquittal
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently directed the Chhattisgarh government to pay ₹30 lakh in compensation to a man who remained in jail for more than seven years after his acquittal in a murder case [Devilal Gond v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors] . A Bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and Sanjeev Sachdeva noted that the acquittal was never communicated to jail authorities. It said that the State’s explanation for the illegal detention revealed “complete remissness on the part of all authorities”. “There appears to be lack of coordination and institutional dysfunction. Appellant lost his prime youth on account of the apathy and lack of promptitude on the part of the authorities,” the Court said in its November 16 judgment. Pertinently, the Court directed all High Courts to consider passing directions similar to those issued by the Madhya Pradesh High Court to prevent such cases in the future. It also called upon the High Courts to set up an online criminal justice platform. “The High Court of Madhya Pradesh has also launched an Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem. The Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem is an integrated platform for Police, Courts, Prisons, Prosecution, Forensics & Hospitals.

items.title: Madras High Court refuses to restrain release of Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion on OTT
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently refused to restrain the exploitation and distribution of the Hindi film Drishyam: The Conclusion , starring Ajay Devgn and Tabu, including its release on OTT platforms, amid a copyright dispute involving the remake rights of the Drishyam franchise [ Rajkumar Theatres Vs Wide Angle ]. Justice PB Balaji dismissed an interim injunction application filed by Rajkumar Theatres Private Limited, which claimed that it held rights to remake the original Malayalam film Drishyam and its sequels in Hindi. The Court held that Rajkumar Theatres had failed to establish a prima facie case of copyright infringement. It also noted that an application under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act in the matter had earlier been dismissed on merits. The Court held that the company could not now seek the same interim relief in a civil suit since the earlier dismissal of the Section 9 application would operate as res judicata against any fresh plea for identical interim relief. " The test is to see whether the relief sought for in the Section 9 application has been decided on merits or not, and if so, then there is a clear, explicit res judicata for operating again

items.title: Former Kerala High Court judge's wife killed after being hit by truck
items.summary: NP Vijayalakshmi, wife of former Kerala High Court Justice PR Raman, breathed her last on Monday after being hit by a concrete mixer truck while crossing a road in Kochi. According to reports , Vijayalakshmi, aged 72, was a resident of Kadavanthra in Ernakulam. She was attempting to cross a road near Kadavanthra signal Junction around 6 PM when the accident occurred. The truck driver, who was waiting for the traffic signal, moved the vehicle forward when the signal turned green. The truck then hit Vijayalakshmi, causing fatal injuries. The Kadavanthra Police which is investigating the circumstances surrounding the accident, has taken the driver into custody and seized the truck. This tragic incident comes amid continuing concerns over road safety in Kochi, where accidents involving heavy vehicles and pedestrians have been recurring with increaing frequency.

items.title: Actress assault: Kerala High Court dismisses plea by survivor's lawyer for contempt action against trial judge Honey Varghese
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday dismissed a plea filed by advocate TB Mini, who represented the survivor in the 2017 actress assault case, seeking contempt of court action against judge Honey M Varghese who conducted the trial and acquitted prime accused Dileep [ TB Mini v The Hon'ble Registrar General & ors ]. Advocate TB Mini had assisted the public prosecutor in the actress assault case and connected matters before the trial court as well as the High Court. The trial in the actress assault case had concluded in December 2025 with the conviction of prime accused Pulsar Suni and five others , while actor Dileep, who was accused of masterminding the assault, was acquitted of all charges. Advocate Mini alleged that during the trial, judge Varghese made certain defamatory statements against her in open court on January 12, 2026, while considering a petition filed on behalf of the survivor actress. The lawyer, therefore, filed a plea before the High Court seeking the initiation of contempt of court proceedings against judge Varghese. The petition challenged the Kerala Advocate General's refusal to grant consent for the initiation of such contempt proceedings on an application earlier
